notes: Skill v1.1.0 (adds blader/humanizer v4 patterns and guards). 9 cases, Opus 5.5, with and without the skill.
Assertions are at ceiling: 63/63 with the skill, 62/63 without. The only baseline failure was the intro growing from 220 to 304 words.
No over-editing: on the clean human-written abstract both configurations returned it byte-identical and said so. All revisions kept every number.

Length is the clearest difference. Revisions with the skill changed length by -44% to +24%; without the skill, by -41% to +92%. The baseline expanded three of the seven revisions by 38-92% (staging discussion 199 to 382 words), adding interpretation and limitations the author never asked for.
Compared with v1.0 (round 2), v1.1 produced shorter revisions on the two shared revision cases (case report 327 to 308 words; intro 151 to 124), so the new guards did not cause over-editing.

New-pattern cases (staging/strawman, LaTeX, reviewer response, author voice, audit) were handled correctly by both configurations; Opus without the skill already avoids these tells when asked to revise. The skill's measurable effect on these cases is restraint in length and consistent placeholders.
